memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For the entrance to the tent make a curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen — the work of an embroiderer. Make gold hooks for this curtain and five posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold. And cast five bronze bases for them." - Exodus 26:36-37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes at the doorway. The entrance to the tent had its own curtain — beautifully embroidered in blue, purple, and scarlet, hung on gilded posts. Even the way in was made lovely. God cared about the threshold, the first thing a priest would see and pass through.

An entrance implies an invitation. However carefully God guarded His holiness, He also provided a way in. The tabernacle was never designed as a sealed fortress; it had a door. From the very beginning, God's intention was that His people would come to Him — carefully, reverently, on His terms, but genuinely come.

Jesus took up this very image when He said, "I am the door" (John 10:9). He is not merely the one who shows the way; He is the way in. Every embroidered curtain, every gilded post, every layer of covering in this chapter was pointing toward a Person who would open the door permanently. If you have been standing at a distance, wondering whether you would be welcome, look at the entrance God has provided. It was made beautiful, and it was made for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I really believe the way to God has been opened for me personally?
Am I standing at a distance when Christ is inviting me to come in?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the door, and through You the way to the Father stands open. Thank You for making a way in. Help me come freely and often into Your presence. Amen.
